title: Expected encoding of a machine step
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $n,s$ be natural numbers, and let $x$ be a Boolean input of length $n$. Let $c$ be a configuration on input $x$ whose work-tape heads lie within distance $s$ of the origin and whose work tapes are blank outside that window. Let $t$ be a codec row, $p$ a tuple of an input-head position and work-head positions, $q$ a case consisting of an optional state, an optional input symbol, and one optional symbol per work tape, and $a$ a Boolean assignment to the codec ports. If the wired port values satisfy the codec guard for $p$ and $q$, then for every codec bit $b$, its expected value under the action determined by $q$ equals its observed value in the successor configuration of $c$ under one step of $M$.
hypotheses_covered: All work-tape heads of $c$ have absolute position at most $s$
